text:
sam: Quick sync — I sketched an ops-readiness checklist for the Optimize toolkit pilot (batching/caching/quant + eval-alerts). Need final gating asks for pilot handoff to SRE. TL;DR: golden prompt set, performance SLI matrix, failover plan to fallback model, and eval-alert thresholds. See list below.

sam: Draft checklist items: 1) Golden prompt set + baseline eval scores; 2) SLI matrix (p50/p95/p99, error rate, cost/per-token delta); 3) Telemetry events and dashboards; 4) Prefix-cache stress tests; 5) Quantization fallback behavior + opt-out flag; 6) Eval-triggered alert rules + playbook; 7) Canary rollout plan and acceptance gates.

maria: This looks solid. Can we add explicit acceptance numbers for latency and acceptable cost regression? Also who signs off on customer-facing docs? :eyes:

cheng: Propose SLOs for pilot (targeting Dedicated-like perf): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms, p99 < 600ms for 8k context on our small-sized pool. Cost goal: cached/batched workload <= 0.9x baseline per-token. Open to adjust after smoke runs.

priya: For eval-triggered alerts: define the golden prompt "pass" metric and the rollback threshold. Example rule: if golden_set.mean_f1 drops > 5% relative to baseline for a 30m window => page + notify on #incidents + flag for manual rollback. We should avoid automatic rollback in MVP.

priya: Example alert rule (draft):
```yaml
alert: optimize_golden_regression
expr: (golden_set_mean_f1 / baseline_f1) < 0.95
for: 30m
labels:
  severity: high
annotations:
  summary: "Optimize toolkit golden set F1 dropped >5%"
  runbook: "See docs/optimize/pilot-eval-playbook.md -> run mitigation steps 1-4"
```

jules: Pilot customers asked for a quantization opt-out per-tenant. We need a runtime flag + console toggle and a note in the onboarding checklist. Can the API layer carry tenant annotations?

eng-oncall-bot: build-bot: Deploy preview (optimize/pilot-readiness) succeeded — build #1023. e2e jobs queued: batch-stress, cache-leak, eval-golden.

sam: +1 on tenant flag. We'll expose: `quant=on|off|auto` and surface recommended profile in Console. For MVP the UI is info-only (no auto-enforce).

sam: Also calling out a "prefix-cache leakage" test: run concurrent eviction/writes for 12h and assert stable mem footprint and hit_ratio >= 75% for steady-state workload. Fail if OOMs or >5% increase in GC pauses.

maria: Let's make an acceptance matrix mapping feature -> tests -> owner -> sign-off. Quick mockup:
- Batching: perf microbench + load test -> cheng -> eng-sre sign-off
- Caching: cache-stress + mem-leak test -> sam -> eng-sre + infra
- Quant recs: UI smoke + fallback tests -> jules -> product sign-off
- Eval-alerts: golden-set suite + paging drill -> priya -> support/ops sign-off

cheng: I'll own telemetry + dashboards. Events I'll instrument: `optimize.batch.size`, `optimize.cache.hit_ratio`, `optimize.cache.evictions`, `optimize.quant.fallbacks`, `optimize.eval.golden_score`. Will stub dashboard tiles and a golden-set time-series.

priya: Rollout gating proposal: canary 1% for 24h (health checks pass) -> 10% for 48h -> 100% full. Health checks: error rate < 0.5%, p99 latency within 2x baseline, golden-set score within -2% of baseline. If any gate fails, automatic halt + manual triage.

sam: To keep pilot scope tight, propose MVP freeze: batching heuristics (auto suggestion + server-side opt-in), prefix caching (read-side caching only), quant recommendation UI (info-only, no auto-apply), eval-triggered alerts (notify + manual rollback). Defer auto-rollback, tenant policy automation, and advanced cross-tenant caching to next phase.

jules: Customers are asking for auto-rollback, but agree deferring to v2. We'll collect feature requests during pilot.

sam: Action items: 1) I'll open a PR with the checklist & acceptance matrix; 2) cheng to add telemetry + initial dashboards; 3) priya to formalize alert rules & runbook; 4) jules to spec tenant flag + Console note; 5) eng-oncall-bot will run e2e suite and report.

sam: Ping me if anything blocks. Planning short sync tomorrow 10:30 to align owners and ship the PR. :rocket:
